business_problem: OMV needs to reduce uncertainty in complex geothermal and carbon capture and storage decisions, while also making large volumes of structured and unstructured subsurface data easier for geoscientists to find, summarize, and use in day-to-day technical work.
solution_summary: OMV is building two complementary in-house AI capabilities for its low-carbon energy business. For geothermal and carbon capture and storage planning, OMV and Stanford University are creating an AI-driven decision-making tool that ingests subsurface and surface operating data and evaluates field-development choices such as where to drill wells, how many wells to drill, when to inject CO2, hydrogen, or cold water, where to place CO2 injectors, and which monitoring techniques to use. The tool acts as a compute layer for simulation-heavy design and safety decisions, helping reduce uncertainty and field-design effort. In parallel, the OMV Energy Chat Bot is being developed with OMV colleagues in Norway to work over large volumes of structured and unstructured subsurface data. It uses GPT/LLM capabilities with knowledge graphs to summarize, extract, and present technical information to geoscientists, turning buried domain data into faster decision support.

solution_components.name: AI-driven decision-making tool
solution_components.role: Analyzes geothermal and CCS field-design choices such as drilling, injection timing, injector placement, and monitoring selection to reduce uncertainty and support safer decisions.

solution_components.name: OMV Energy Chat Bot
solution_components.role: Provides geoscientists with summarized, extracted, and presented technical information from OMV's subsurface knowledge base.

solution_components.name: knowledge graphs
solution_components.role: Organize technical knowledge so the chatbot can retrieve and connect domain-specific information for geoscientists.

data_flow: OMV feeds structured and unstructured subsurface and surface data into two AI paths. The decision-making tool analyzes reservoir and field-design variables to recommend drilling, injection, injector-placement, and monitoring choices for geothermal and CCS projects. In parallel, the OMV Energy Chat Bot uses GPT/LLM processing over domain data linked through knowledge graphs, then serves summaries, extracted facts, and technical presentations to geoscientists for project execution and decision-making.
integration_points: Structured and unstructured subsurface and surface data
Carbon capture and storage monitoring workflows
business_outcome: OMV says the AI approach reduces uncertainty, improves safety and risk assessment, lowers field-design and operational costs, speeds project execution, improves information quality, and supports more profitable low-carbon business development.
